sections.heading: Pull request — exfer-indexer #2 (closed)
sections.text:
feat: index EXFER-QUOTE settlement datums (issue #28 Wave 3, stage 1)

Wave 3 **Stage 1** (critical path) of the EXFER-QUOTE honor layer (ahuman-exfer/exfer#28). Teaches the indexer to observe the `quote_id`-in-datum settlement link, so an acceptor (exfer-swap) can find a settlement by `quote_id` and confirm what it binds. The indexer stays **read-only** and holds no per-identity honor state — that lives in exfer-swap (later stages).

## What
- **Strict settlement-datum decode** (`extract.rs`): an inline output datum is a `quote_id` **iff it is exactly 16 bytes** — no trailing bytes, no multi-id, no length-prefix. Full-equality only, never substring/prefix. Closes the **F1** double-deliver class found in the Wave 3 adversarial review (a 4096-byte datum embedding two quote_ids → one payment satisfying two quotes).
- A **`datum_hash`-only** output (no inline datum) is recorded **UNHONORABLE** and never falls back to address+amount matching (closes **M2**).
- Two redb tables: **`OUTPUT_DATUM`** (outpoint → quote_id | unhonorable, O(1)) and **`DATUM_BY_QUOTEID`** (quote_id → all outpoints; secondary-index idiom shared with `HTLC_BY_HASHLOCK`; reports every outpoint — the swap-side gate enforces 1:1). Both participate in reorg `wipe_above`.
- Two RPCs: **`get_output_datum`** and **`find_settlements_by_quote_id`** (full-equality; rejects non-16-byte ids at the API boundary).
- `schema_version` bump triggers an automatic **from-genesis reindex** to backfill the new tables (per-block apply is idempotent); documented in README.

## Decision
Locked by maintainer: the settlement datum is the **bare 16-byte quote_id, nothing else** — this tightens the issue #28 spec ambiguity that enabled F1.

## Tests
`cargo build` / `test` / `fmt --check` / `clippy -D warnings` all green — **44 tests**. Covers strict-decoder edge cases (0/1/15/16/17/32/4096 bytes), index-and-find, oversized-not-indexed, datum_hash-unhonorable, and reorg wipe.

## Next stages (exfer-swap)
Durable seen-set + consumed-outpoint gate, then the HTLC and plain-output honor branches that consume these queries.
